You are a repo fix worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo (/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory) at HEAD — edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own exactly two paths: factory/outbox_push.py and tests/test_outbox_push.py. Nothing else — do not touch outbox_listen, reescalate, or the other outbox test files. Never touch .git, never commit, never run git add; leave changes uncommitted. The harness stages every change and FAILS on anything outside your two owned paths.

CONTEXT: factory/outbox_push.py is the mailroom leg that turns department outbox rows into a Telegram ping, a Linear card, a ledger row (which the hourly re-arm job needs), and a buttons buzz. PROVEN DEFECT, reproduced in production 2026-08-05T21:00Z: in tick(), after the plain ping succeeds, a card-sender failure is only LOGGER.warning'd ('card sender failed for %s line %d') and execution falls through to state['last_hashes'] append + state['offset_lines'] = line_index + 1 — the row is CONSUMED with no card, no ledger row, and no buttons. The owner got one plain text and the escalation became permanently unreachable. A Linear API TimeoutError swallowed the first real escalation from a just-revived department manager.

CHANGE (minimal, in tick()): when card sending is enabled for the watch and the card sender fails, the row must NOT be consumed — do not append the digest to last_hashes, do not advance offset_lines, LOGGER.error (upgrade from warning) with the same message content, and break out of this watch's line loop so the same row is retried on the next tick, preserving in-order delivery per watch. Deliberate consequences you must preserve and document in a short comment: (1) during a Linear outage the plain ping repeats each tick for the stuck row — that repetition IS the loud outage signal, matching the estate's refile-louder rule; (2) a buzz-sender failure AFTER the card and ledger row exist keeps consuming the row exactly as today (the ledger row makes the card re-armable, so a lost buzz is a delay, not a loss); (3) ping-sender failure behavior (error + break, not consumed) is already correct — do not change it; (4) ledger append behavior unchanged. Also count card failures and, mirroring how ping failures influence the exit code (read how exit code 3 is derived), make the process exit nonzero when any card send failed this tick so systemd shows red — reuse the existing exit-code convention rather than inventing a new one if a suitable one exists.

TESTS: extend tests/test_outbox_push.py in its existing style (it stubs senders as argv fixtures): (a) card sender fails => cursor file shows the row NOT consumed (offset unchanged, digest absent from last_hashes), no ledger row appended, and the run exits nonzero; (b) next tick with a working card sender => card created, ledger row appended, digest recorded, offset advanced — the retry delivers; (c) buzz failure after successful card+ledger => row IS consumed (regression-pin the delay-not-loss contract).

HOW TO RUN (from the worktree root — all must pass): PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_outbox_push.py tests/test_outbox_push_buzz.py tests/test_outbox_push_stall.py -q -p no:cacheprovider && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 loopfactory.py check

HARD RULES: no new dependencies, smallest possible diff, keep deny-by-default (never consume on an undelivered card), no reformatting of untouched lines, never invoke any network, model CLI, MCP, or skill, and leave changes uncommitted — the harness exports the diff.
